subject: Elements of fit-measures in lavaan with endogenous categorical variables

messages.author: c6f28689f4eb93ea
messages.subject: Elements of fit-measures in lavaan with endogenous categorical variables
parts:
Dear members,
I did a path analysis (two equations) in lavaan (only manifest variables) with one categorical endogenous variables. I know, that lavaan doesn't support margins (of the change of an unit of independent variabels on the probability of the dependent categorical variables). But what about the common fitmeasures (goodness of fit) of a probit regression: Pseudo-R^2 of McFadden, Loglikelihood-indices and LR-Test? Is it possible to get a report within lavaan, which contains such elements?
What is the command? If I prompt the command "lavInspect(m1.fit, "r2")", I get the R^2. But are these R^2 the Pseudo-R^2? I think now, they are rather the normal R^2 for the linear association of the independent variable x and the variable z, which mediates between x and y? (I know that it is possible to get these fitmeasures  in association with the glm-command in R, but how does it work in lavaan?)?

Thank you
Jürgen

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Elements of fit-measures in lavaan with endogenous categorical variables
parts: Pseudo-R^2 of McFadden, Loglikelihood-indices and LR-Test?

These are all calculated from log-likelihoods, which are only available using ML estimation.  lavaan does report R^2 on the latent-response metric, which is McKelvey & Zavoina's pseudo-R-squared.

https://stats.idre.ucla.edu/other/mult-pkg/faq/general/faq-what-are-pseudo-r-squareds

You can still use the lavTestLRT() function to conduct a (scaled/shifted) chi-squared-difference test, which is a LRT when the models'  chi-squared values are each a LRT.

An alternative is pairwise ML (estimator = "PML"), but that would not enable calculating the (full-)likelihood-based pseudo-R-squareds because it is a product of all uni- and bivariate likelihoods.  But the lavTestLRT() function nonetheless provides corrected information criteria.

https://users.ugent.be/~yrosseel/lavaan/pml/PL_Tutorial.pdf
